headerDescription: End-to-end, production-ready image classification pipeline using pre-trained ResNet-50 weights. Demonstrates backbone freezing, classification head replacement, data pipeline optimization, and multi-stage fine-tuning.
subtitle: Deep Residual Network for Vision Tasks

snippets.code:
import tensorflow as tf
from tensorflow.keras import layers, models
from tensorflow.keras.applications import ResNet50

# 1. Load Pre-trained ResNet50 Backbone (weights trained on ImageNet)
base_model = ResNet50(
    weights='imagenet',
    include_top=False,
    input_shape=(224, 224, 3)
)

# 2. Freeze the Base Backbone to preserve pre-trained representations
base_model.trainable = False

# 3. Construct Custom Classification Head
inputs = layers.Input(shape=(224, 224, 3))
x = tf.keras.applications.resnet50.preprocess_input(inputs)
x = base_model(x, training=False)
x = layers.GlobalAveragePooling2D()(x)
x = layers.BatchNormalization()(x)
x = layers.Dropout(0.3)(x)
outputs = layers.Dense(10, activation='softmax', name='classifier')(x)

model = models.Model(inputs, outputs, name='ResNet50_Transfer_Learning')

# 4. Compile Model with Adam Optimizer and Categorical Crossentropy
model.compile(
    optimizer=tf.keras.optimizers.Adam(learning_rate=1e-3),
    loss='categorical_crossentropy',
    metrics=['accuracy']
)

# 5. Summary & Training Verification
model.summary()
print("✓ ResNet50 Transfer Learning Pipeline successfully initialized.")

import tensorflow as tf

def build_data_pipeline(data_dir, batch_size=32, img_size=(224, 224)):
    """Builds an optimized tf.data pipeline with prefetching and GPU caching."""
    dataset = tf.keras.utils.image_dataset_from_directory(
        data_dir,
        image_size=img_size,
        batch_size=batch_size,
        label_mode='categorical'
    )
    
    # AUTOTUNE prefetching for zero I/O bottleneck
    autotune = tf.data.AUTOTUNE
    return dataset.cache().prefetch(buffer_size=autotune)

import numpy as np
import tensorflow as tf
from tensorflow.keras.preprocessing import image

def predict_image(model, img_path, class_names):
    """Loads a target image, applies ResNet preprocessing, and predicts class probabilities."""
    img = image.load_img(img_path, target_size=(224, 224))
    img_array = image.img_to_array(img)
    img_batch = np.expand_dims(img_array, axis=0)
    
    # Apply exact ResNet50 input preprocessing
    preprocessed_img = tf.keras.applications.resnet50.preprocess_input(img_batch)
    
    # Perform batched inference in evaluation mode
    predictions = model.predict(preprocessed_img)
    top_class_idx = np.argmax(predictions[0])
    confidence = predictions[0][top_class_idx]
    
    print(f"Predicted Class: {class_names[top_class_idx]} ({confidence * 100:.2f}% confidence)")
    return class_names[top_class_idx], confidence

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
from torchvision.models import resnet50, ResNet50_Weights

# 1. Load Pre-trained ResNet50 Weights
weights = ResNet50_Weights.DEFAULT
model = resnet50(weights=weights)

# 2. Freeze all feature extractor parameters
for param in model.parameters():
    param.requires_grad = False

# 3. Replace Final FC Head for 10 custom classes
num_features = model.fc.in_features
model.fc = nn.Sequential(
    nn.BatchNorm1d(num_features),
    nn.Dropout(0.3),
    nn.Linear(num_features, 10)
)

# 4. Device Placement & Optimizer
device = torch.device("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")
model = model.to(device)
criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(model.fc.parameters(), lr=1e-3)

print(f"✓ ResNet50 initialized on {device}. Classifier parameters active.")

import torch
from PIL import Image
from torchvision import transforms
from torchvision.models import resnet50, ResNet50_Weights

# 1. Setup Inference Transforms & Model
transform = ResNet50_Weights.DEFAULT.transforms()
model = resnet50(weights=ResNet50_Weights.DEFAULT)
model.eval()

# 2. Perform Single Image Forward Pass
@torch.no_grad()
def infer_single_image(img_path):
    img = Image.open(img_path).convert('RGB')
    tensor_input = transform(img).unsqueeze(0)  # Shape: [1, 3, 224, 224]
    
    logits = model(tensor_input)
    probabilities = torch.softmax(logits, dim=1)
    top_prob, top_catid = torch.topk(probabilities, 1)
    
    return top_catid.item(), top_prob.item()

callouts.title: Why Freeze the Backbone?
callouts.content: Freezing lower convolutional layers preserves low-level visual primitives (edges, textures, shapes) learned from millions of ImageNet samples. It prevents initial noisy gradients from damaging pre-trained weights while training a newly initialized classification head.

callouts.title: Common Mistakes in Transfer Learning
callouts.content:
1. Forgetting to set training=False on BatchNormalization layers during inference or transfer learning.
2. Omitting framework-specific input normalization (e.g. resnet50.preprocess_input), which causes scale mismatches between [-1, 1] and [0, 1].

callouts.title: Production Tip: Two-Stage Fine-Tuning
callouts.content:
Stage 1: Train only the top classifier head for 3–5 epochs with learning rate 1e-3.
Stage 2: Unfreeze top ResNet bottleneck blocks (e.g. conv5_block) and fine-tune with a 10× to 100× smaller learning rate (1e-5) to avoid catastrophic forgetting.

bestUsedWhen: Custom image classification tasks with small-to-medium labeled datasets (<50,000 samples).
Establishing a reliable, fast baseline before exploring heavier ViT or ConvNeXt backbones.
Scenarios demanding fast real-time CPU/GPU inference with low latency constraints.
tradeoffs: Slightly lower Top-1 accuracy (74.9%) compared to modern ViT-Large or ConvNeXt architectures.
Requires input images to match the standard 224×224 resolution unless fully convolutional mode is used.
Batch normalization statistics require careful synchronization across multi-GPU distributed nodes.
expectedBehavior: Rapid initial loss drop within the first 3–5 epochs during top-head warmup training.
Stable convergence during Stage-2 unfreezing with reduced learning rate (1e-5).
Gradient flow is stabilized across all 50 layers via identity skip connections.
deploymentNotes: Seamlessly exports to ONNX, TensorRT, and TensorFlow Lite with FP16/INT8 quantization.
Keep Batch Normalization layers locked in inference mode during production deployment.
Specify explicit input tensor signatures (e.g. [1, 224, 224, 3]) for low-latency serving.

strategy.rationale: Training a 50-layer CNN from scratch requires >1.2M labeled images and extensive compute. Initializing with ImageNet-1k pretrained weights grants high-level visual primitives (textures, edges, shapes) from epoch 0.
strategy.backboneStrategy: Freeze all convolutional stem and residual bottleneck layers (requires_grad=False / trainable=False). Prevents random classifier gradients from destroying low-level pretrained feature maps.
strategy.fineTuningStrategy: Execute 2-stage training. First train newly attached classification head for 3-5 epochs, then unfreeze top bottleneck block (conv5_x) with a 10x-100x lower learning rate.

trainingProgression.description: Train custom FC/dense classifier while keeping ResNet backbone fully frozen.
Unfreeze stage4/conv5 bottleneck blocks; fine-tune with reduced learning rate.
Optional: Unfreeze all 50 layers with discriminative learning rates for large domain datasets.

trainingConfig.checkpointStrategy: Save Best Top-1 Accuracy Model Checkpoint
